subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What aspects of the films are reviewers focusing on?

judge.implied_focus: The film aspect/dimension a review focuses on (acting, plot, directing, visuals, music, dialogue, effects, atmosphere, humor)

per_column.name: focus_acting
per_column.rationale: Binary flag for whether the review focuses on acting -- a coherent facet of the film-aspect focus.

per_column.name: primary_focus
per_column.rationale: Categorical roll-up naming the single dominant aspect per review; directly names the inferred focus variable and ties the binary facets together.

judge.rationale: All added columns centre tightly on ONE coherent, data-inferable focus concept: which aspect of the film a reviewer emphasizes. The nine binary facet flags enumerate a well-differentiated, mutually consistent set of film dimensions at a useful granularity, and primary_focus provides a categorical roll-up that both names the proposed focus and resolves the dominant aspect per review. This is a genuine multi-facet decomposition rather than a single restatement or generic noise (no bare length/token/sentiment padding). The focus is directly actionable: an analyst can quantify which aspects dominate reviews and cross them with label_pos. Minor deductions: some facet-flag distributions are thin (e.g. effects_technical=12), and a 'general' catch-all in primary_focus slightly dildilutes sharpness, but the structure is strong.
